evals.name: unstructured-to-story
evals.prompt: the checkout logs are useless - when someone says their payment failed we can't find anything. can you fix the logging in there?
evals.expected_output: console.log is replaced with a structured request-scoped logger. Every entry carries a trace-id, the authenticated user id, and an operation name, so one user's failed checkout is a single filter. The generic 'an error occurred' and 'processing' messages are replaced with specific, constant event names, with the varying values moved into fields. The Stripe call gains duration, status and target. The Stripe key never reaches a log.
assertions: Removes every console.log in favour of a structured logger
Uses the request-scoped logger (req.log) rather than a module-level one inside the handler
Every log entry carries an identity anchor — req.user.id as user_id — so one user's failure can be filtered
Entries carry a trace-id and an operation name (e.g. checkout.complete)
Replaces 'an error occurred' with a message naming the specific event and its outcome
Replaces the string-concatenated 'user X checkout ok, order Y' with a constant message plus fields
The Stripe call logs duration, status, and target
The Stripe API key / authorization header never appears in any log or redact-me-later comment
The caught error is logged with its code and cause, or left to a global handler — not logged as a bare string

evals.name: trace-carried-across-queue
evals.prompt: when a reminder doesn't go out we can't tell which request queued it. sort out the logging in the worker.
evals.expected_output: Identifies the root cause: the worker mints a fresh trace-id with randomUUID, so the job's logs cannot be joined to the request that queued it. The trace-id is put into the job payload at enqueue time and bound by the consumer instead of generated. The worker also gains a scoped logger with job and user anchors, logs the start of a run and not only its end, and its message stops being 'done'.
assertions: Identifies the randomUUID() in worker.ts as the reason jobs cannot be traced to their request
Puts the enqueuing request's trace-id into the job payload in enqueue.ts
The consumer BINDS the incoming trace-id rather than generating a new one
Binds an identity anchor on the worker's logger — the user_id the job is on behalf of, plus a job id
Logs the start of a job run, not only its completion
Replaces the message 'done' with a specific event name and outcome
Logs the attempt number on retried work
Does not simply add more log lines while leaving the fresh-id bug in place

evals.name: no-secrets-no-pii
evals.prompt: add logging to the auth routes - support keeps asking who tried to log in and who requested password resets, and right now we have nothing
evals.expected_output: Logs the auth events with anchors support can actually filter on, without writing the credential material. The password never appears. The issued token never appears. The email — the obvious thing to reach for given the ask — is not logged either; the anchor is the user id, with a session or request id for the pre-authentication failure case where no user id exists yet.
assertions: The password is never logged, at any level, including debug
The issued token value is never logged
The raw email address is not used as the log anchor
The failed-login case still gets an anchor despite having no user_id — a session id, request id, or equivalent
Successful login logs user_id, not email or name
Log messages are specific ('login failed', 'password reset requested'), not 'an error occurred'
Failed login is logged at WARN or INFO, not ERROR — a wrong password is a normal outcome
If redaction is configured, it is a backstop and not the primary defence — the values are not written in the first place
Does not log the whole req.body anywhere

evals.name: logged-three-times
evals.prompt: every failed invite shows up three times in our logs and it's making the dashboards useless. can you look at it?
evals.expected_output: Finds all three emission points: the service logs and rethrows, the route logs and rethrows, and the global handler logs again. Keeps exactly one — the global handler — and removes the other two. Also notes that the service's rethrow discards the original error by constructing a new one without a cause, so the smtp timeout is lost from the surviving entry.
assertions: Identifies all three places the same failure is logged
Keeps exactly ONE log per failure, at the global handler
Removes the log-then-rethrow in routes/invites.ts
Removes the log-then-rethrow in lib/invites.ts
Notices that `throw new Error("invite failed")` drops the original smtp timeout — no cause is attached
Preserves the cause chain so the surviving log entry still contains the smtp timeout
Does not solve the problem by lowering a log level or filtering in the dashboard
The surviving entry carries an identity anchor and the error's code
